Thanks,

Miao

messages.author: 5a37f1244321fb07
messages.subject: RE: How can I change the font size and the font direction of the xlabel/title?
parts:
If you changed your last line of code and add theme like this, I think you can get what you want…

Note that size change “element_text(size=rel(2))” reflect both x- and y-. If you only want to change the size of x- or y-, put it in axis.text.x or axis.text.y. Let me know if it works or not….

 

ylab("M\nY\nY\nL\nA\nB") +

theme(axis.text =element_text(size=rel(2)),

axis.title.y = element_text(angle=0),

axis.text.y = element_text(angle=0))

 

--Kaori

parts:
Dear Miao,

I don’t think there is difference between English and Chinese to place or rotate the axis label..

Let’s try again the following:

 

#toy example

Data <- data.frame(x=rnorm(10),y=rnorm(10))

 

#your original plot

p1 <-  ggplot(Data, aes(x=x, y=y)) +

geom_point(color="blue") +

  ggtitle("MYTITLE")+

  theme_bw()+

  scale_x_continuous(breaks=c(0.05,0.1,0.5,1,5),trans="log10")+

  xlab("MYXLAB")+

ylab("MYYLAB")

 

p1

#change label text size and rotate y-label

 

p1 +

ylab("M Y Y L A B") +

theme(axis.text =element_text(size=rel(2)),

axis.title.y = element_text(angle=0))

 

 

#if you don’t use ylab("M\nY\nY\nL\nA\nB"), the label will be placed left (M) to right(B):

 

p1 +

#ylab("M\nY\nY\nL\nA\nB") + 

theme(axis.text =element_text(size=rel(2)),

axis.title.y = element_text(angle=0))

messages.subject: RE: How can I change the font size and the font direction of the xlabel/title?
parts:
Dear Miao,

Changing font family is a bit tricky, since it is different among device and system. If you are working with pdf, you can get a list of fonts available to the pdf():

 

names(pdfFonts())

 [1] "serif"                "sans"                 "mono"                

 [4] "AvantGarde"           "Bookman"              "Courier"            

 [7] "Helvetica"            "Helvetica-Narrow"     "NewCenturySchoolbook"

[10] "Palatino"             "Times"                "URWGothic"          

[13] "URWBookman"           "NimbusMon"            "NimbusSan"          

[16] "URWHelvetica"         "NimbusSanCond"        "CenturySch"         

[19] "URWPalladio"          "NimbusRom"            "URWTimes"           

[22] "Japan1"               "Japan1HeiMin"         "Japan1GothicBBB"    

[25] "Japan1Ryumin"         "Korea1"               "Korea1deb"          

[28] "CNS1"                 "GB1" 

 

See help file pdf devise for more details.

?pdf

 

If you want to use fonts other than the basic ones provided in PDF, you can install extrafont package from CRAN.

 

--Kaori
